30: | Paper and figures | Draft Chinese paper and figures in `runs/R23/execute/paper/` | Only results accepted by the relevant receiving gate | Every number/claim maps to raw source or accepted result; figures have units and source; pending values stay visibly pending; render-check final reader format |
39: | 2. Freeze model experiment | Before scores, define reference and alternative formulas, folds, outcome metrics, candidate-selection rule, interval recipe, solver settings/tolerance, resource limits, and sensitivity questions in a versioned config. Choose origins mechanically from data availability: enough history for the 56-day baseline and complete 42-day labels by the cutoff; use at least two selection origins and a later untouched holdout when the authorized history permits. Record any missing fold and its consequence before fitting. | Frozen config and fold list; forecast worker input | If fewer than two valid selection folds or no untouched 42-day holdout exists, do not claim a reliable ranking; report the feasible descriptive comparison and uncertainty. Never move a fold after seeing scores. |
43: | 6. Compare and challenge | Score fixed candidates on identical chronological folds. Report point metrics (MAE/RMSE/bias), 90% coverage/width, shortage/waste/combined loss, spend, capacity use, and runtime only when measured. Test only material sensitivities: uncertainty sample choice/quantile behavior, fictional event multiplier, weather only if an admissible published forecast route is proposed, and resource constraint perturbations. | Metrics, plots, targeted sensitivity results, interpretation notes | If the alternative does not improve the predeclared criterion, retain the current route and explain the tradeoff. If a sensitivity changes ranking or plan materially, qualify conclusions and include it. No post-holdout tuning. |
44: | 7. Generate 42-day outputs | At the fixed origin `2026-10-31 18:00`, refit the selected eligible method on the final as-of snapshot; create all 4,032 forecast rows and 4,032 plan rows for Nov 1–Dec 12. Forecast and replenishment are separate tables, each key includes method identity. | `future_predictions.csv`, `future_replenishment.csv`, `decision_summary.csv`, lineage and reproduction manifest | Enforce 42×96 unique keys in both tables, same key set/method, finite point/lower/upper values, ordered interval endpoints, exact `interval_level`, integer `q`, and every daily constraint. Future actual demand is never needed or scored. |
54: | `replenishment.csv` | `service_date,store_id,item_id,method_id,q_units`; integer, nonnegative; same keys/method as predictions |
64: Preflight checks source availability, Python package/runtime needs, writable output domain, and whether an independent reader is actually available. A green preflight is not a result. The first smoke is the probe in `probe.py`: one complete 96-pair future date, one complete historical 96-dimensional residual window, nominal interval fields, integer optimizer output, source timestamps, and original daily constraints. It only demonstrates plumbing and one feasible computed plan under its chosen scenario sample. The current version emits `probe-output-v2/scenarios.csv` and `feature_lineage.csv` so a receiver can recompute the output and inspect the timestamp boundary; the earlier output remains retained in `probe-output/`.
66: Full acceptance requires a frozen, reproducible 42-day result, every requested comparison and explanation, exact constraint/objective recomputation, source-time integrity, uncertainty caveats, paper-to-result traceability, and independent receiving review. Keep producer self-checks, accepted outputs, and independent verdicts as separate states. If evidence is incomplete, label it pending or blocked at the affected branch; do not lower a gate, invent missing measurements, or convert a design/probe into completed production.
